item.title: Jack’s Old-Time Jam — Wed Sep 9, 5:00 PM — Jack Of The Wood
item.description:
Grab some dinner and a pint while enjoying our long-running Old-Time Jam! Featuring many talented musicians from the local WNC area, our traditional Appalachian mountain music jam runs from 5-9pm every Wednesday night at Jack of the Wood! Jack Of The Wood is still a downtown hot spot for food, brews and drink since 1997 and founders Joan and Joe Eckert who still own it, have maintained the original lively English and Irish vibe. The old-time mountain and Irish music jams continue, including a hot bluegrass jam Thursdays and brunch every Sunday. The venue extends a welcoming feeling to regulars and newcomers to this day. https://jackofthewood.com/
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Jam > Grass > Jam: The Saylor Brothers — Wed Sep 9, 6:30 PM — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
The Saylor Brothers are a jamgrass fusion group from Asheville, fronted by brothers Will & Ben Saylor, of Brushfire Stankgrass. This project is a foray further into the realm of bluegrass jam, with more emphasis on improvisation piled on top of a structure of traditional bluegrass and innovative original songwriting. As a trio with Greg Stiglets on bass, the band packs a large sound coming from three acoustic instruments, and often adds a fourth player for further improvisational and bluegrass firepower.
Jam > Grass > Jam is not an open bluegrass jam but is a residency featuring a rotating casts of special guests from Asheville’s bluegrass/jamband scene.
French Broad River Brewery is more than just a place to enjoy a drink—it’s a community hub where great beer, delicious pizza, live music, and good times come together. item.description: The Queen Sessions at Hotel Eve | A celebration of the legendary women who shaped jazz. Hotel Eve proudly presents The Queen Sessions, a concert series curated by Melissa McKinney, honoring the iconic voices that defined generations of jazz. Each Wednesday evening features a rotating lineup of Asheville’s premier vocalists, each bringing their own style, artistry, and interpretation to the music of legends like Ella Fitzgerald, Billie Holiday, Nina Simone, Sarah Vaughan, Dinah Washington, Abbey Lincoln, and more. No two performances are alike. Every week offers a fresh cast of artists & new collaborations. Saara Maria (Saara Sallinen) is an Asheville-based vocalist known for her rich, soulful tone and versatility across jazz, neo-soul, R&B, and intimate acoustic settings. item.title: Asheville Crokinole Club — Tue Sep 15, 6:00 PM — Taproom At Highland Brewing Co.
item.description:
Crokinole Tuesdays at Highland Brewing Taproom Join us every Tuesday in the Taproom for an evening of flicks, strategy, and friendly competition! We’re hosting the Asheville Crokinole Club—a community of players who love this classic dexterity board game. Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out! Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just curious, come grab a pint, meet new friends, and test your skills.
Source: Highland Brewing

item.title: Fall Tree ID — Sat Sep 26, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Fall Tree ID With Lauren Lampley Friday, September 26 | 1 – 4pm BRN – Core | BREG – Elective Register Here!
Join this class as we discuss how to use different characteristics and field guides to identify common trees of Western North Carolina found here at the NC Arboretum. We will look at using different characteristics including habitat, bark, buds, growth pattern, leaf shape, and fruit/nut shape to identify trees. This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. item.title: Experiential Learning Fair — Tue Sep 29, 3:00 PM — Cowpie Lawn
item.description:
The Experiential Learning Fair (or ELF) is a tabling event where majors and crews come together to highlight the super cool experiential learning they are doing. It gives students an opportunity to explore other major and crew options, as well as faculty/supervisors an opportunity to try and recruit new folks to their work.
Source: Warren Wilson College
